Every substantive page declares `title`, `description`, `audience`, `status`,
and `last-reviewed`. Mark incomplete work visibly as `planned`; do not fill a
gap by copying an unverified historical OPAL chapter.

## Local preview

```bash
quarto preview --profile opalx
```

The `opalx` profile targets the production `OPALX-project/opalx-manual` and
`OPALX-project/opalx-documents` repositories. For a one-off private fork, copy
`_quarto.yml.local.example` to
`_quarto.yml.local` and set its `documents-base-url`. The local file is ignored
by Git.

## Release manuals

The site root always shows the development manual built from `main`. Each OPALX
release series is published beside it in `<major>.<minor>/`, for example `1.0/`,
and a *Manual release* selector in the sidebar switches between them on the
same page.

Pushing a tag `OPALX-<major>.<minor>.<patch>` renders that commit, attaches the
HTML site as `opalx-manual-site.tar.gz` to the GitHub release of the tag, and
redeploys `main`. Every deployment unpacks these archives with
`scripts/assemble_release_sites.rb`; release manuals are never rebuilt. The
highest patch tag of a series replaces its directory. The script also writes a
`versions.json` into every manual directory, which the selector reads at
runtime, so an older release learns about newer ones.

A tag runs the workflow stored at the tagged commit. Before tagging, the commit
should pin links that would otherwise follow `main`: set `documents-base-url`
to the matching `opalx-documents` tag and limit `book.repo-actions` to
`[issue]`. Local previews have no `versions.json` and show no selector.

## PDF publication (paused)

The build workflow currently publishes HTML only. `BUILD_PDF` is `"false"` in
`.github/workflows/build.yml`, so PDF dependencies, rendering and validation are
skipped. `_quarto.yml` sets `book.downloads: []` to hide the unavailable book
download. External report PDFs remain available through their existing links.

To restore PDF publication, set `BUILD_PDF` to `"true"` and restore
`book.downloads: [pdf]`. Keep the conversion tools installed before the render
step. Explicit local PDF builds remain available with the prerequisites below.

The PDF build needs a TeX distribution, headless Chrome for Mermaid diagrams,
and `rsvg-convert` for SVG figures. Install the conversion and inspection tools
before rendering; HTML rendering does not exercise SVG-to-PDF conversion.

On Ubuntu, as used by the build workflow:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install --yes librsvg2-bin poppler-utils
```

On macOS with Homebrew, the corresponding packages are `librsvg` and `poppler`.
With TeX installed, prepare the diagram renderer and build the book explicitly:

```bash
quarto install chrome-headless-shell --no-prompt
rsvg-convert --version
quarto render --profile opalx --to pdf --no-clean
ruby scripts/validate_rendered_pdf.rb
```

## Linking binary documents

Place OPALX presentations, reports, examples, and datasets in the category-first
`opalx-documents` tree. Link them only through project metadata:

```markdown
[OPALX overview]({{< meta documents-base-url >}}/presentations/2026/features/2026-04-06-opalx-overview.pdf)
```

Project metadata supplies `documents-base-url`, so page content does not embed
repository locations directly.

Report summaries live in the nested `resources/reports/` Quarto project. Add a
detail page beneath its year directory and link it from
`resources/presentations-reports.qmd`; do not add individual reports to the
numbered book chapters. The nested archive is rendered after the main HTML site
and shares the selected deployment profile.

## Asset policy

PDFs, Office documents, archives, and media are rejected from the manual.
Raster figures must remain at or below 500 KiB. Source SVG, TikZ, Mermaid,
small plots, and reproducible text scripts may remain with the page they
support. Generated Quarto output is never committed. The separately hosted
[Doxygen API reference]({{< meta doxygen-url >}}) is linked rather than copied
into this manual.
